verdict.rationale: ObsessionDB documents its own agent-access path: MCP connections authenticate via OAuth 2.1 instead of API keys, agents run on isolated read-only compute, and roles can scope access down to table and column. Together these give agents constrained credentials. However, the evidence never shows a user explicitly minting a scoped or least-privilege credential bound to a specific agent; the table/column roles are documented in an SSO-login context, not tied to agent tokens. Missing for 10: explicit docs on issuing per-agent scoped tokens or OAuth scopes, a link between table/column roles and agent credentials, token lifecycle details (expiry, revocation), and independent or hands-on corroboration.
